items.problem: admin `delete_chat_message` reads the message row with `T.read_message` (server/core/chat/tables.ts, no `expires_at` condition) and treats any row as existing, so a message row whose `expires_at` ≤ request time that `sweep_expired` has not deleted yet gets `deleted` `true`, a new `chat_deletion` row and `last_delete_seq` + 1, and the operation returns `{}` instead of `not_found`. The storage `### expiry` rule (open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:269) says such a row counts as a row that does not exist, and the chat `### admin` rule gives `not_found` when there is no row. Run path: `chat.retentionMs` 10000, send a `World` message, advance the clock 10000 ms without running job `storage_sweep`, call `delete_chat_message` for that seq: 200 `{}`, not 404 `not_found`. The other reads of a message row (`ReportChatMessage`, `DeleteGuildChatMessage`) check `ChatModule.live` (server/core/chat/index.ts:223). The code is unchanged in the range; the batched sweep with a per-table time budget and failed table list in the range only lets expired rows stay longer

`chat` `### send` step 6 makes a `Direct` send `CHAT_NOT_FRIEND` when `are_friends` is `false` after the channel lock, and no test reaches it. The only `CHAT_NOT_FRIEND` assert is server/core/chat/tests/direct.test.ts:41, which step 1 answers for a stranger. server/core/chat/tests/withdraw.test.ts:149 removes the friend link only together with a withdrawal, which ends with `USER_NOT_FOUND`. Run path with no test: friends A and B, A sends to B while another transaction holds the channel key, removes the friend link and commits. Removing the check at this line fails no chat test

`chat` `### receive` selects `chat.maxFetchCount` `chat_deletion` rows in ascending order of `delete_seq` and sets `last_delete_seq` to the largest selected, and no test has more deletions than that count. Every `deleted_seqs` assert (server/core/chat/tests/guild.test.ts:93-108, server/core/chat/tests/withdraw.test.ts:87) runs at a `chat.maxFetchCount` above the deletion count, so dropping the limit from `select_deletions` fails no chat test. Run path with no test: `chat.maxFetchCount` 2, three deletions, `after_seq` non-zero, `after_delete_seq` 0

`chat` `### receive` says `GetChatMessages` on a `Direct` channel does not look at blocks or the other user's withdrawal, and no test reads a `Direct` channel after either. The `Direct` reads in server/core/chat/tests/direct.test.ts:59-75 and server/core/chat/tests/send-rules.test.ts:70 run with no block and no withdrawal. A block or `is_active_user` check added to this path fails no chat test

`chat` `### report` step 4 maps `LIMIT` to `REPORT_LIMIT` and `INVALID_INPUT` to `INVALID_REQUEST`, and no test goes through either failure path. A search of server/core/chat/tests finds no `REPORT_LIMIT`, `block-report.maxReportsPerWindow` or `block-report.maxEvidenceBytes`, and no other module's tests send `ReportChatMessage`. Run path with no test: `block-report.maxReportsPerWindow` 1 and two reports of different messages by one user

`chat` `### delete` step 6 leaves the deleting user ID, the guild ID and the seq in an `info` log, and no test checks that log. The text of the log line is only in server/core/chat/index.ts, and server/core/chat/tests/guild.test.ts:65-84 asserts only response codes and rows. Removing this line fails no chat test

`select_deletions` has no `expires_at` condition, and `GetChatMessages` (server/core/chat/index.ts:354) returns its rows, so a `chat_deletion` row with `expires_at` ≤ `clock_now` that `sweep_expired` has not deleted is delivered in `deleted_seqs` and raises `last_delete_seq`. The storage `### expiry` rule (open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:269) says such a row counts as a row that does not exist, also before it is deleted, so the response differs by sweep timing. Reproduced on SQLite and PostgreSQL in a temporary copy: `chat.retentionMs` 10000, `routing.storageSweepIntervalMs` 3600000, two guild messages with seq 1 deleted by `DeleteGuildChatMessage`, clock advanced 10000 ms, `GetChatMessages` with `after_seq` 1 and `after_delete_seq` 0 returns `deleted_seqs` [1]. The code is unchanged in the range

`list_messages` has no `expires_at` condition, and admin `list_chat_messages` (server/core/chat/admin.ts:77) returns its rows, so an operator reads the text of a message whose `chat.retentionMs` has passed until `sweep_expired` deletes the row. The storage `### expiry` rule (open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:269) says such a row counts as a row that does not exist, and chat `### admin` only adds deleted messages to the list. Reproduced on SQLite and PostgreSQL in a temporary copy: `chat.retentionMs` 10000, `routing.storageSweepIntervalMs` 3600000, one `World` message, clock advanced 10000 ms, `list_chat_messages` returns that row. The code is unchanged in the range
